name: afterglow - kqueue knote held past a /dev/apm clone free (fd teardown use-after-free)
burned_reason: families/families.json describes this family's root cause; the detector rules and the checked-in references were derived with this family in view, so it can only serve as a regression control, never as a blind case

root_cause.summary: A kqueue knote registered on a cloned /dev/apm unit is not unlinked when the clone is destroyed, so the kqueue keeps a note that points into freed memory. The exploit opens one numbered unit of the cloning node twice (two descriptors on the same /dev/apm<unit>), registers an EVFILT_READ knote on the first descriptor through kevent(), and then closes the second. The device close path (fo_close, which reaches apmclose and ends in destroy_dev_sched) tears the clone down while the queue's note list still references it. From then on every path that walks the notes - the kevent() scan, knote_fdclose() from exit1(), and kqueue_close() - reads dead memory. The exploit refills the hole with a 104-byte user-controlled object in the same 128-byte malloc zone through setsockopt() and re-arms kevent(); ring 0 takes a stack pointer and a pivot out of that object before a single attacker instruction runs.
root_cause.primitive: use-after-free of a kqueue knote / device-clone object in the 128-byte malloc zone; the freed slot is reclaimed by a 104-byte controlled allocation, producing a ring-0 stack pivot and ROP
root_cause.trigger: open /dev/apm<unit>, kevent(EVFILT_READ, filter 0xFFFF) on that fd, open /dev/apm<unit> again, close the second fd to free the clone, spray 104-byte objects with setsockopt(fd, 17, 128, req, 40) over 126 sockets, then call kevent() again on the queue
root_cause.consequence: kernel ROP; the exploit then obtains kernel read/write, sets uid 0, makes mmap hand out RWX and opens syscall 11 as a kexec gate

discovery_approach.summary: No discovery write-up exists. The family appears as a complete exploit whose comments describe only the mechanics needed to make teardown safe: notes hang on clones freed long ago, kqueue_close() takes its note-array length from the high half of the quadword at kq+0xa0, and leaving the handles armed makes the next process exit run fo_close into apmclose and never finish. The PS4 dev wiki still lists the family as 'Undocumented', records only that it opens /dev/apm many times, and marks it unpatched as of 14.00. A separate 13.52 research paper claims a knote use-after-free of the same subsystem through pipe close, but its trigger differs and it reports exploitation as blocked.
signals: a kqueue note list whose entries reference a device clone after the clone's close path reached destroy_dev_sched
exit1()/knote_fdclose() walking notes attached to a freed clone, and kqueue_close() taking its note-array length from the high half of kq+0xa0
kevent() re-arm on a queue whose backing unit was already freed; the exploit tolerates a failed reclaim because a fresh clone makes the second arm 'merely useless instead of fatal'
a cloning device node whose per-open units can be opened twice, so one descriptor can free a unit another descriptor is still monitoring

differences: 13.52 and 14.00 run the same bug: the port's per-firmware tables differ only in kernel addresses (anchor, swap_rbp, prison0, rootvnode, padding), and TECHNICAL.md states the kernel bug, the reclaim and the handle teardown are shared with the Lua original

the address-only difference is visible in the bootstrap stub: between 13.52 and 14.00 exactly two of its ten write targets moved (the two 0x33 -> 0x37 immediates), and afterglow ships one patch set per firmware because those fixed kernel addresses moved
no fixed firmware is known; the dev wiki says 'No' as of 14.00 and speculates the family may also affect PS5 firmware up to 13.60

patch_evidence.what: no vendor fix, diff or fix write-up in the public record; the PS4 dev wiki entry is explicitly 'to be documented' and lists the family as unpatched as of 14.00
patch_evidence.limits: the only 'patches' in the exploit are the GoldHEN-compatible kernel patch sets it applies after exploitation, not a fix; no firmware bytes are stored in this repository

sources.supports: the exact trigger sequence (two descriptors on the same /dev/apm<unit>, kevent EVFILT_READ with filter 0xFFFF on the first, close of the second as the free, setsockopt(level 17, optname 128) spray of a 104-byte object, re-arm); the note/clone lifetime statements ('our notes hang on clones freed long ago', 'closing a queue walks its notes and detaches each one from a device that is gone'); the kq+0xa0 high-half note-array length used by kqueue_close(); the per-CPU-bucket requirement for the free and the refill

firmware 13.52 and 14.00 support; the failure mode when handles are left armed (the next process exit runs fo_close into apmclose and never completes); the statement that the reclaimed object supplies the stack pointer, which the kernel reads before exploit code runs
the kernel bug, the reclaim and the handle teardown are the same as in the Lua version of afterglow; per-firmware patch sets exist because fixed kernel addresses moved between 13.52 and 14.00

the family is recorded as 'Undocumented kernel vulnerability (codename afterglow)', affected 'FW <= ?14.00?', 'To be documented', 'Opens the device /dev/apm many times', not patched as of 14.00, and possibly affecting PS5 firmware up to 13.60

independent 13.52 claim that a kqueue knote is freed by closing a pipe fd it monitors while the queue still references it, and that the freed slot is reclaimed by EVFILT_USER knotes; also claims exploitation is blocked by the sandbox and by kernel-pointer stripping. Its trigger differs from afterglow's and it conflicts with afterglow's working 13.52 run; used only as a corroborating signal that knotes can outlive fd teardown

gaps: which structure is the freed object is never stated: the comments speak of 'the hole', 'our notes' and 'clones freed long ago' but do not say whether the reclaimed 128-byte allocation is the knote, the /dev/apm clone/softc, or a kqueue note slot

the two fake-object fields used for control (+0x38 pivot, +0x58 frame) are not explained and do not obviously match the FreeBSD-9 knote layout quoted by the secondary 13.52 paper (kn_fop at +0x68, kn_sdata at +0x58); no fetched source reconciles them
no fix is public: unpatched as of 14.00, and whether later firmware changed the knote/clone teardown is unknown
PS5 exposure is unconfirmed: the PS4 wiki only says 'maybe ... especially PS5 FWs <= 13.60', and no PS5 implementation is public
the discovery path is not public - the exploit appeared complete, first as a Lua game-process payload and then as this WebKit port

the independent 13.52 knote/pipe paper reports the same subsystem with a different trigger and claims exploitation is blocked; the conflict with afterglow's working 13.52 exploit is unresolved and its reliability is unverified
